svg.title: Nerve injury: after ruling out a tendon or blood-flow cause, localize the lesion (radiculopathy versus mononeuropathy) from the pattern of sensory loss and weakness, then grade it by the Seddon classification (neurapraxia, axonotmesis, neurotmesis), which predicts recovery; electrodiagnostic studies confirm, localize and grade

svg.text: Electrodiagnostic studies (EDX) = nerve conduction studies (NCS) + needle electromyography (EMG)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • NCS: SIZE of the response = axon health · SPEED = myelin health

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • EMG: is the muscle quiet at rest (denervated muscle is not)? does it fire on command? which muscle exactly?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • Answers: is it a nerve, where, how bad (myelin or axon, in continuity?), the likely timeline, or a muscle problem (myopathy)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • NOT for musculoskeletal pain (rotator cuff tear) or central nervous system disease (stroke)
